facts: The accused was convicted under Section 302 IPC for brutal multiple homicides in a rural dispute. The trial court and High Court awarded the death sentence. On appeal to the Supreme Court, counsel argues that the sentencing judge did not properly record special reasons or weigh mitigating circumstances such as age and possibility of reformation under Section 354(3) CrPC before imposing capital punishment.
issues: Whether the imposition of death sentence satisfies the rarest of rare doctrine and mitigating factor balancing test.

facts: A state government enacted facial recognition surveillance at public transit hubs without statutory backing. A citizen petitioner challenges the surveillance program under Article 32, claiming it infringes informational privacy, bodily autonomy, and freedom of movement without satisfying the three-fold proportionality test.
issues: Whether mass facial recognition surveillance without legislation violates the fundamental right to privacy under Article 21.

facts: A chemical fertilizer manufacturing plant leaked toxic gas into neighboring residential colonies, causing respiratory illnesses and environmental contamination. The factory owners claim force majeure and sabotage by third parties, disclaiming strict liability. Victims file a writ petition demanding restitution and compensation under Article 21.
issues: Whether an enterprise carrying on hazardous activities is subject to absolute liability without common law exceptions.

facts: The district administration issued an indefinite blanket ban on broadband and mobile internet services under Section 144 of the CrPC to maintain public order. Journalists and online merchants argue this arbitrary restriction infringes their freedom of speech, expression, and trade under Article 19.
issues: Whether indefinite suspension of internet services violates freedom of speech under Article 19(1)(a) and the proportionality doctrine.
